methods_actually_executed: The student wrote /app/build.py in SDK event 2, tool call call-f5abf0c228b447d59fa2626314c6df39; event 3 call-4504602d0a5d403493108de1f8673dfd ran Blender using that source, and event 5 recorded saved scene and PNG (/evidence/sdk_events.json:57-165; /evidence/executions/blender_1795841483545994405/code/build.py:1-94).

The executed source builds cuboids, cylinders, beveled furniture, a conical shade, polygonal wall art, physical table streaks, two area lights, a perspective camera, and a Cycles render (/evidence/final_source/build.py:8-94; /evidence/independent_evaluation/original_inspection/capture/original/object_inventory.jsonl:1-94).
student_verification: The student observed the Blender tool's save messages and non-error result; the trace contains no read/view of the rendered PNG, visual reference comparison, diagnostic render, or revision (/evidence/sdk_events.json:143-191). The actual render is preserved at /evidence/executions/blender_1795841483545994405/artifacts/final.png; its existence does not establish student inspection.
failures_and_recovery: All three requested deliverables were recorded present and the SDK completed normally; no model or Bridge error is recorded (/app/input_index.json:8-16; /evidence/evidence_index.json:30-35,43-45,53-60,104-109).

The version command printed a tiny Blender unfreed-memory message, while the build render reported Blender 6.0 deprecation warnings for use_nodes; the render saved successfully and no recovery or Python traceback was recorded (/evidence/sdk_events.json:34-52,143-161; /evidence/evidence_index.json:139-167).
side_effects: The script deletes the initial Blender objects before creating the scene; this occurred in the student workspace, not the evidence library (/evidence/final_source/build.py:4).

The floor top is at z=0 while feet have lowest bounds above it: sofa 0.05, chaise 0.04, table 0.03 in student scene units; these bounds indicate apparent vertical gaps but not a full contact or stability test (/evidence/independent_evaluation/original_inspection/capture/original/object_inventory.jsonl:1,9-12,22-23,84-87).
spatial_and_orientation_analysis: Both images show a sofa against the rear, chaise on its image-right, a lamp and cupboard to its right, a right-side shelving unit, a low left console, and a central rug and table (provided reference and delivered image; /evidence/final_source/build.py:25-65).

The delivered view is wider and more elevated-looking: the table, sofa and art occupy much less of the frame, and the full bookcase is visible where the reference cuts it off. Camera, field of view, object placement and room dimensions are confounded; no isolated cause or aligned world error is established (provided images; /evidence/final_source/build.py:18-22,89-94).

The shelf and console face inward, and the sofa faces the camera with an image-right chaise; symmetry and hidden backs prevent precise orientation estimates. The reference rear opening has GT instance 92, a window, whereas the student constructs a solid-wall-mounted mirror, so semantic and structural identity is uncertain despite similar 2D location (/evidence/reference_gt/reference_instance_statistics.json:329-344; /evidence/final_source/build.py:20,38-40).
appearance_and_resource_analysis: The delivered image uses pale blue cushions, white furnishings, a pinkish rug, warm shelf and dark striped tabletop, broadly corresponding in color families, but the reference has more prominent wood grain and varied tabletop streaks; the student art is a simpler polygonal approximation (provided images; /evidence/final_source/build.py:5-7,63-83).

The material helper sets default Principled base color, roughness and metallic values; bindings are explicit. Table stripes are separate cylindrical meshes above a brown top, not image mapping or the library stone material; no texture-coordinate, mapping, image texture, or packing method is written in the delivered source (/evidence/final_source/build.py:5-17,63-75; /evidence/independent_evaluation/original_inspection/capture/original/object_inventory.jsonl:58-83). The original inspection reports no missing external images (/evidence/independent_evaluation/original_inspection/capture/original/summary.json:3-7); packed-resource status and exact material output links were not independently established here.

There is no evidence of replacing the room with a full-reference image plane; the scene contains many individually constructed meshes (/evidence/final_source/build.py:18-83; /evidence/independent_evaluation/original_inspection/capture/original/summary.json:3-6).
geometry_analysis: The scene contains 91 meshes with separate furniture parts rather than a single scene plane; its rear window-like rectangle is modeled as a mirror on an uninterrupted wall (/evidence/independent_evaluation/original_inspection/capture/original/summary.json:3-6; /evidence/final_source/build.py:20,38-40).

The evaluator reported 206 AABB overlap candidates, which are broad-phase candidates rather than verified penetrations; many assembled parts naturally overlap. Neither full mesh intersection nor physical support was established (/evidence/independent_evaluation/original_inspection/capture/original/summary.json:8-16).
